deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is the first sheet of Riemann's philosophical fragment 'Antinomien', a reworking of Kant's antinomies (Critique of Pure Reason, Transcendental Dialectic). The page is laid out in two columns, Thesis and Antithesis, across four numbered rows.

Header. Thesis = the finite (Endlichkeit/Endliches), the representable (Vorstellbarkeit). Antithesis = the infinite (Unendlichkeit), conceptual systems lying at the boundary of the representable ('Begriffssysteme, die an der Grenze des Vorstellbaren liegen').

I. Thesis: finite (simple) elements of time and space. Antithesis: the continuous (Stetiges). This is the only mathematically relevant row. It is Kant's second antinomy (simple parts versus infinite divisibility), recast as discrete versus continuum.

II. Thesis: freedom. It is defined not as Kant's faculty of beginning a causal series absolutely, but as the capacity to decide between two or more given possibilities. Riemann argues as follows. For decisions by free choice (Willkür) to be possible despite completely determinate laws governing the action of representations (Vorstellungen, in a Herbartian sense), one must assume something about the mental mechanism. It must have, or at least reach in its development, the ability to bring about the necessity of such decisions. Antithesis: determinism. The right column has several cancelled attempts at a sentence ('Niemand kann ... die Überzeugung aufgeben, dass die Zukunft durch sein Handeln ... bestimmt werde ...'). It ends unfinished: 'Niemand kann sich angesichts der ...'.

III. Thesis: a God acting and changing in time (world-governance, Weltregierung). Antithesis: a timeless, personal, all-knowing/all-mighty, all-good God (providence, Vorsehung).

IV. Thesis: immortality. Antithesis: a thing-in-itself underlying our temporal appearance, which shapes its own intelligible character through transcendental freedom (and, probably, 'radical evil'). This uses Kant's vocabulary throughout.

Closing paragraph (left, bottom). Freedom is entirely compatible with strict lawfulness of the course of nature. But the concept of a timeless God is not tenable alongside it. The limitation that omnipotence and omniscience suffer through the freedom of creatures must be compensated by assuming a temporally co-acting God, a guide of events and of human destinies. So the concept of providence must be supplemented by the concept of world-governance. A marginal note at the bottom right reads roughly 'nachgestaltende Erlösung/Erziehung (Einzelner)'.

The next page carries on with the 'general relation of the conceptual systems of thesis and antithesis'. There Riemann ties the Antithesis (the continuum) to Newton's limit method: a finite number of intermediate stages, whose number is then increased until the gaps between them tend to zero.
errors: No mathematical steps to check. On the philosophical side, Riemann's claim that freedom (as choice among given possibilities) is compatible with strictly deterministic laws of representation is asserted, not argued. The mechanism ('the mental mechanism reaches the ability to bring about the necessity of the decisions') is only sketched, and the Determinismus column is broken off mid-sentence.

results.what: Recasting Kant's antinomies as finite/representable (thesis) versus infinite/continuous conceptual systems at the limit of representability (antithesis), with row I as discrete elements versus the continuum.
results.modern_name: Kantian antinomies; discrete vs. continuum (Kant's second antinomy)
results.usually_credited_to: Kant (1781); this reworking is Riemann's own

results.what: Freedom as choice among given possibilities, held compatible with strict natural law, while a timeless God is rejected in favour of a God acting in time (world-governance supplementing providence).
results.usually_credited_to: Various (Leibniz, Kant, Herbart, Fechner); this text is Riemann's

deep.surprise_reason: This is the 'Antinomien' fragment, printed by Weber and Dedekind in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke among the philosophical fragments of the Nachlass. It is purely philosophical and contains no new mathematics. Its content (Herbartian psychology, Kantian vocabulary, Fechner-like theology) is known to Riemann scholars.
transcription_corrections: Header: probably 'Thesis (Endliches) Vorstellbares' and 'Antithesis (Unendliches)', matching the Werke text 'Endliches, Vorstellbares' / 'Unendliches'.
Row IV: 'durch transscendentale Freiheit, durch radicales Böses' is more likely than 'durch selbst Böses[?]'. The printed version speaks of 'radicales Böse'.
Row III, right column: the word above the line reads 'allmächtiger'/'allwissender' as a correction. The list is roughly 'zeitloser, persönlicher, allwissender (allmächtiger), allgütiger etc.'.
Closing paragraph: 'Annahme eines zeitlich mitwirkenden Gottes' is more likely than 'geistig mitwirkenden[?]', given the contrast with 'zeitlos'.
Closing paragraph: 'durch die Freiheit der Geschöpfe' should be read as one phrase. The insertion is 'der Geschöpfe', and '(im Sinne)' is uncertain.
The bottom-right marginal note may read 'nachgestaltende Erziehung (Einzelner)' rather than 'Erlösung'. Uncertain.
Row II: '{+eine plötzliche Änderung+}' is very uncertain. The insertion may instead be 'eine plötzliche Entstehung' or similar.
